quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other driver may need your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have better escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle can block your way to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: Is hearing protection important for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Not recommended.
Recommended only for long rides.
Recommended for all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Recommended for all rides.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet on. Use hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can most safely handle road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Together with the rear brake.
It is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What can happen if a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast?

options.text: They will have better control of their motorcycle.
They will experience a more stable ride.
They may unintentionally leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may unintentionally leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn or curve too fast can cause you to lose control. Your motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: Which color makes you less visible to other drivers?

options.text: Orange
Yellow
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green to be more visible. Avoid dark or dull colors while riding.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: Appearance
Protection
Price

questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection is most important when buying a helmet. Choose a helmet that fits well, fastens securely, and meets DOT safety standards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black symbols warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign tells you the right lane will end soon.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use only your front brake.
Use only your rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both the front and rear brakes at the same time with controlled pressure.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a passenger vehicle's brake light.

options.text: More noticeable than
Just as noticeable as
Not as noticeable as

questions.correctAnswerText: Not as noticeable as
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are usually not as bright as car brake lights. Other drivers may not see your brake light right away. Stay aware of this when braking.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:

options.text: Bright clothing.
Dark clothing.
Clothes that are uncomfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to make yourself more visible to other drivers. Reflective clothing is even better and helps during the day too.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped on the side of the road while using its flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it more space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Grabbing at the front brake or jamming down on the rear brake:

options.text: Can cause the brakes to lock.
Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down when the streets are wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the brakes to lock.
questions.explanation: Squeezing the front brake hard or slamming the rear brake can lock the wheels. This causes loss of control.

questions.question: Eye protection:

options.text: Is not necessary if your motorcycle is equipped with a windshield.
Is only necessary when riding in bad weather.
Should allow the rider a clear view to either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should allow the rider a clear view to either side.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper eye or face protection. Your protection must allow you to see clearly to both sides. A face shield protects your whole face in a crash.

questions.question: To properly control a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Allow your feet to hang off the footrests.
Sit so your arms hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent. Use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced during turns.

questions.question: When preparing to ride with a passenger, instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get onto the motorcycle before you.
Sit as far back as possible.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.
questions.explanation: Have your passenger get on after you start the engine. They should sit forward, close to you, and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: How can you make sure other drivers see you?

options.text: Wear bright clothing.
Wear dark clothing.
Follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. Reflective material also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider look for in a protective jacket?

options.text: Black or another dark color.
Warmth.
Leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or strong synthetic material. It should cover your arms, fit snugly, and allow you to move freely. Look for one with built-in body armor for best protection.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid confusing other drivers?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after completing a turn or lane change.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal once you finish turning or changing lanes. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your original lane?

options.text: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane is slippery when wet because of oil buildup. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest option.
